title: An Old Song at Sea
subtitle: A gritty song, infused with the hues of a coral reef and a hint of brine.

trails.title: Last-Second Scramble
trails.description: Knowledge is power! Quickly, find the creature's weakness before you get killed!

content.text:
Serres

Common Names: Pig-toothed Ray, Anchor Fish, Deep Bass Disc, Hammerhead Ray.

    Back home, we call this thing a Sea Bat.

    That's not right! Sea Bats are a different species and they definitely don't smash your portholes at night!

Classification: Subclass: Aquatic Primal Critter, Order: Oceanic, Family: Ray-form, Genus: Flying Ray.

    In my opinion, it should be classified as a bird.

Distinctive Features: Broad wings, long tail, a pair of clawed fins, and curved ivory-white fangs.

    Hey, I just thought of a business idea! Could we pass these fangs off as ivory?

    Serres typically live in groups and feed on large fish, seabirds, and drifting debris. While they may look similar to Olitiau, their behavior couldn't be more different. While Olitiaus are generally non-aggressive, Serres are known for their fondness for challenging creatures larger than themselves—including sperm whales, baleen whales, megalodon sharks, and passing ships. Sometimes, they even mistake protruding rocky outcrops and coral reefs for foes. When a Serres spots a ship, it leaps from the water, attacking the vessel with its sharp wings and calling upon its companions. They seem to have a competitive nature; each Serres strives to soar higher and leave deeper marks on its target.

    Stay away from the windows. You never know how deep their wings can slice.

    Despite their large numbers, Serres communicate through a single method: sound. They can produce a wide range of calls within the 10-180Hz frequency range, ideal for underwater communication, and they can sense each other's vibrations through their wing membranes. The best way to deal with Serres is to disrupt their hearing. Shouts, bangs, and music can confuse them, while enough volume can physically irritate their auditory systems, causing them to flee in discomfort.

    Now that's more like it! My former captain tried using anti-Olitiau measures against them, which is why he's my "former captain."

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: I've learned so much about the outside world since I boarded this ship, so ...

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Why do I feel even more confused?

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: I trust my people. They're good and kind, and they've never lied to me.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: You just have to look at their Spirit Shells to see it. The songs and dances of Meli nourish the Shells, and the purity of my people's souls color their surface in the most beautiful patterns.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: And Ms. Grace, she's been good to us, too.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: She warned us about the destruction of Meli, saving us from the flood. And she showed us the world as it really is.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: She even wants us to be part of her plan.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Our ancestral shells have also told us how terrible the world outside is—that it's a place with sanguma witches, Nakarua serpents, and all kinds of other beasts.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: But ...
Those scenes replay again and again in her mind.
The casual conversations, the warm smiles, and the glowing lamps in their hands.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: But now I'm here, on this ship full of outsiders, and I feel that they're just like us.
Past and present blur together as Fatutu searches her memories, leaving her dizzy and overwhelmed.
In her daze, she has wandered into another part of the ship. It isn't until a voice snaps her out of her thoughts that she realizes where she is.

items.speaker: Helmsman Esam
items.text: Hello, young lady! What are you doing out here all by yourself?

items.speaker: Helmsman Esam
items.text: Don't just stand there. Come on in!

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Hmm?

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Sorry, I didn't even realize where I was going.
One helmsman gives her a hearty pat on the shoulder.

items.speaker: Helmsman Charlie
items.text: No need to apologize, my dear.

items.speaker: Helmsman Charlie
items.text: You're more than welcome. You've saved us old folks from sitting here in silence till we reach shore.

items.speaker: Helmsman Giovanni
items.text: Haha! Charlie's just happy to have someone new to tell his stories to!

items.speaker: Helmsman Charlie
items.text: I bet Esam will jump at the chance to show off how he drives off those Serres, too.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Serres? I've heard they're a real headache for passing ships.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: But I've never seen one with my own eyes.
Fatutu curiously peers out the window.
A strange yet familiar hum fills the air.

items.speaker: Serres
items.text: *roar*

items.speaker: Helmsman Charlie
items.text: Well, well, it seems this young lady knows a thing or two about the sea!

items.speaker: Helmsman Esam
items.text: How about you give us a hand, eh?
He extends a rough hand to her.
Fatutu takes a hasty step back, but the hand remains warmly held out before her.

She has seen many hands like his before. Callused, working hands, like those of Grandma Penu, Uncle Tarek, Grandpa Natano, and many of the other Nukutai. There's something comforting in its familiarity.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Me? I'm not sure I know how to ...

items.speaker: Helmsman Charlie
items.text: Don't worry. It's almost too easy!

items.speaker: Helmsman Giovanni
items.text: These Serres are afraid of loud noises, and the "Free Breeze" has plenty of speakers on board!

items.speaker: Helmsman Giovanni
items.text: The sea is with us today.

items.speaker: Helmsman Esam
items.text: Of course it is! For how long we've sailed its waves, why wouldn't it be?
The helmsmen exchange a few winks and shoulder pats. There is a clear camaraderie between them.
They roll up their sleeves as they prepare for their performance.

items.speaker: Helmsman Esam
items.text: Get ready, folks! Port the helm!

items.speaker: Helmsman Esam
items.text: Course 270, hard starboard!

items.speaker: Helmsman Esam
items.text: Slow down to five knots. Watch the bow wave!

items.speaker: Helmsman Esam
items.text: Turn on the speakers! Time to chase off some sea monsters.
The seasoned navigator issues a steady flow of instructions.
The cruise ship slowly turns, skillfully avoiding the reach of the sea monster's "tentacles."

items.speaker: Helmsman Giovanni
items.text: Little girl!
He gives Fatutu a harmonica and asks if she can play it.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Uh ... No ...

items.speaker: Helmsman Charlie
items.text: Don't worry. Anything you play will do. Can't be worse than what Esam has to offer.

items.speaker: Helmsman Esam
items.text: I can hear you, you know!
The sailors joke and jostle as they clamor for their respective instruments.

items.speaker: Helmsmen
items.text: I grieve to leave my comrades all.
They burst into song.

items.speaker: Helmsman Esam
items.text: Come on, join in!
The harmonica finds its way to her lips.
Melodious music, off-key yet heartfelt, drifts out toward the sea.
This is just like those nights by the bonfire in Meli.

items.speaker: Helmsmen
items.text: But a poor simple sailor just like me,

items.speaker: Helmsmen
items.text: Must be tossed and turned in the deep dark sea.

items.speaker: Helmsmen
items.text: Farewell to Nova Scotia, the sea-bound coast.

items.speaker: Helmsmen
items.text: Let your mountains dark and dreary be.

items.speaker: Helmsmen
items.text: For when I'm far away on the briny ocean tossed,

items.speaker: Helmsmen
items.text: Will you ever heave a sigh or a wish for me?

items.speaker: Serres
items.text: *roar*
One nameless sea shanty after another tears through the fog, with lights shimmering on the sea's surface like embers after a festival bonfire.
Realization strikes her. She finally understands her role.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Ms. Grace!

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: The outside world is indeed full of dangers, but there is less to fear than you think.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: I'll help you through it.
Advice and reassurances echo in her mind. She suddenly feels weak.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: What am I doing?!

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Sorry, I have to go.

items.speaker: Helmsman Esam
items.text: Hm?
She scurries off.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: I don't understand.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Why are they so nice? This is nothing like the stories.
Her questions hang in the air, and so too does a knuckle at a door.
Come in.
Guest Room

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper, I hope you didn't have too much difficulty during the power outage.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Not at all, Sonetto. It actually gave me the opportunity to try out X's latest invention—the Bouncing Bulb.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's very interesting, a little draining though.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Would you like to try out one of these, then?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Did you make this, Sonetto?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I did. Ms. Selone from Nukutaeao taught me how to make it. It's called a Sea Mother's Eye.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: She told me every household in Meli lights them during storms to help guide those at sea safely home.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: She said, "With this, no one will ever be lost in the dark."

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Thank you, Sonetto. And what a lovely saying.
Sonetto breathes a sigh of relief, but her eyes remain fixed on the Sea Mother's Eye.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: After this mission, we should be able to apply for a field investigation in Italy.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Italy?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Thank you, Timekeeper.
Sonetto is unable to hide her delight.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But let's focus on this mission first.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: May I borrow your communicator?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: There's something I need to verify.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Of course.

items.speaker: Communicator
items.text: *beep*

items.speaker: Communicator
items.text: Connecting to Madam Z of the St. Pavlov Foundation.

items.speaker: Communicator
items.text: *static*

items.speaker: Communicator
items.text: *buzz*

items.speaker: Communicator
items.text: The person you're trying to reach is currently unavailable due to communication interference. Please leave a message after the beep.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Huh?

items.speaker: Communicator
items.text: *buzz*

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Just as I suspected. Communications are blocked.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Someone's jamming the signal.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Do you think it's Manus Vindictae?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's possible. The flyer proved that this ship has some kind of association with them. We need to stay vigilant.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Regulus should know about this. I'll go find her.
A heart-wrenching scream echoes from afar, reverberating through the halls of the ship.
NOOOO!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Regulus!
They hurry over to the source of the scream.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Regulus! Are you alright?!
Sonetto stops in her tracks.
The scene before her is all too familiar, for it has played out countless times at the LSCC.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Ahem, beautiful day, isn't it?
Ignoring the fact that Regulus just dropped her sunglasses, Ulrich calmly pours coffee into his energy intake.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Mr. Ulrich? What are you doing here?
The ferrofluid swirls in a distorted arc.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Ahem. Good day, Timekeeper, Researcher Regulus, Ms. Sonetto.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Is this really the disguise you went with?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Wait a minute!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Vertin, did you know he'd be here?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Listen, there's no way I'm paying for even half an extra ticket. In fact, he should be paying for me!

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Well, this might take a while to explain.
